title: add-sensitive-data-declassification-flow-rbac-and-kms-quarantine-gateway
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Introduces declassification operator role + KMS quarantine gateway. Adds RBACv2 templates and migration script. Backwards compatible behind feature flag. Requires policy rollout and operator credential update.
description: Motivation: customers in regulated industries asked for a controlled declassification workflow for sensitive outputs (PII/PHI) that ties RBAC v2 role constraints to KMS usage auditing and a quarantine path before plaintext export. This PR implements an end-to-end flow: 1) a new operator role (declassification.operator) with minimal privileges; 2) an in-path KMS Quarantine Gateway that records and throttles requests that would export plaintext after declassification; 3) RBAC v2 policy templates, a migration helper to convert legacy bindings to the new role, and structured audit events for the declassification decision. Design highlights: the gateway is feature-flagged (rbac_v2_declass_flow) and defaults to opt-in. The Gateway emits a signed audit envelope for every declassification decision and attaches a quarantine token to responses when manual review is required. KMS usage is recorded with an explicit "quarantine" tag to prevent accidental key-scoped metrics leakage. Backwards compatibility: when the feature flag is off the runtime behaves as today. Migration: an idempotent migration script updates operator bindings in small batches and emits an audit reconciliation record. Checklist: - [x] API: add new RBAC role and policy schema - [x] Runtime: implement KMS Quarantine Gateway and token plumbing - [x] Auditing: structured events and envelope signer - [x] Migration: script and Linear ticket linking - [x] Tests: unit + integration + end-to-end with fake KMS - [x] Docs: docs page + console role mapping UI strings Limitations and open questions: manual-review UX is out of scope for this PR (see PM-708); we surface a quarantine token and audit id for downstream tooling. Operational notes: when rolling out at scale enable the gateway in monitoring-only mode for 48 hours to validate event volumes and KMS tag cardinality. See linked_linear for tracking work and SUP ticket for a support playbook.

ci_checks: Checks: unit (pass), lint (pass), integration (pass on rerun), e2e (initial failure due to flaky fake_kms - rerun passed), security-scan (pass), policy-linter (pass). Notes: e2e had an intermittent timeout on first run; fixed by increasing fake_kms handshake timeout in handler_test.go and re-running the job.
operational_playbook: Rolling guidance: enable rbac_v2_declass_flow in monitoring-only mode for 48h, confirm audit envelope counts match staging baseline, then enable enforcement. Update operator credentials using tools/migrations/migrate_declass_bindings.py in 500-binding batches and watch for migration-audit events. If KMS tag cardinality spikes, flip feature flag to monitoring-only and roll back the migration by re-running the script in dry-run mode.

notes_for_ops: Requires RBAC v2 enabled. Feature flag: rbac_v2_declass_flow. If using dedicated/private deployments, ensure audit-envelope signer key is present in cluster secret manager before enabling enforcement.
qa_notes: Test matrix included in ci/e2e/declass_flow_test.yml. Scenarios: permissive mode, monitoring-only mode, enforcement mode, migration dry-run. Use examples/fake_kms to simulate key failures and slow responses.
security_review: Completed by SecOps on 2025-11-08. Findings: ensure signer key rotation policy is in place; added guidance to docs. No blockers.
impact_summary: Adds guarded declassification path to prevent accidental plaintext export. Operational cost: small increase in audit event volume and one lightweight gateway hop for declassification paths only. Expected latency impact: +8-18ms p95 on declassification calls in enforcement mode (benchmarked in integration tests).
